name: A Jackson Hole lot

place_source.title: Wikidata: Jackson (Q871285), coordinate location (P625) and elevation above sea level (P2044)

blurb: A suburban lot on the valley floor of Jackson Hole, 1,901 m up in the Snake River headwaters: lawn, sagebrush-edge garden and cottonwood shade under the Tetons, with magpies and ravens by day, mule deer at the fence, and chorus frogs on the spring nights.

facts.text: Jackson has a humid continental climate (Köppen Dfb), with warm summers and very cold winters, in a narrow valley that gets more snow than most of Wyoming.

source.title: Wikipedia: Jackson, Wyoming
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Jackson, Wyoming", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Jackson stands at 6,237 feet (1,901 m) above sea level on the floor of Jackson Hole.

source.title: Wikidata: Jackson (Q871285), elevation above sea level (P2044)

facts.text: The National Elk Refuge, created in 1912, borders the town of Jackson and hosts an average of 7,500 elk each winter on 24,700 acres of meadows and marshes.

source.title: Wikipedia: National Elk Refuge
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "National Elk Refuge", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Flat Creek, a tributary of the Snake River, flows out of the refuge and runs through the town of Jackson.

source.title: Wikipedia: National Elk Refuge
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "National Elk Refuge", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The most abundant birds on the refuge are red-winged blackbirds, magpies, crows and ravens; 47 mammal and 147 bird species have been documented there.

source.title: Wikipedia: National Elk Refuge
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "National Elk Refuge", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
